title: Structural Traps — Bottlenecks and Capacity Constraints
metadata_mapping: Existing concept and responsive asset conventions; no new schema, navigation, or publication action.

patterns.title: Bottlenecks and Capacity Constraints
patterns.domain: Dependency and feasibility traps, with stock-and-flow accumulation and feedback hypotheses

sources.title: Goldratt Research Labs, Introduction to Theory of Constraints
sources.supports: Goldratt’s early-1980s development of TOC; Five Focusing Steps: identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, and reassess.
sources.boundary: Practitioner exposition of the framework. Universal weakest-link rhetoric is not adopted as a theorem about every network. No success-rate estimate or financial-throughput claim is taken from this page.

sources.title: John D. C. Little (1961), A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
sources.supports: Original theorem connecting mean number in the system, mean time, and arrival rate with explicit stationarity, finite-mean, and arrival-process assumptions.
sources.boundary: Original scan opened and read, including theorem assumptions and discussion. It does not estimate a growing café backlog or prove that discarding work creates processing capacity.

sources.title: Cathy Wu, MIT 1.041/1.200, Queuing Models, Spring 2026
sources.supports: Service rates, queue storage versus service capacity, stationary analysis, M/M/1 assumptions and mean-wait formula.
sources.boundary: Official teaching material. No airport example, survey statistic, or universal utilization target is imported into the café scenario.

sources.title: AWS Builders’ Library, Avoiding Insurmountable Queue Backlogs
sources.supports: First-person Amazon engineering account of backlog accumulation, long recovery, and admission/backpressure controls.
sources.boundary: Operational specialist experience in asynchronous software systems, not a controlled study or measured effect size for staffing a physical café.

patterns.short_description: Identify which required activity limits completed output, match incoming work to sustainable capacity, and reassess the whole workflow after changing the constraint.
use_when: What must change to increase completed drinks?
goals: Recognize the concrete predicament before terminology.
Preserve defining assumptions and distinctions without calculations.
Evaluate intervention authority, costs, residual risks, and changed assumptions.
mechanisms: Increase usable preparation capacity or change accepted load, then reassess the whole process.
Staff and equipment cost money. Same machine access may prevent parallel work; quality and handover capacity remain.

example_structure.scenario: Every accepted drink order requires payment, preparation, and handover. Preparation is currently limiting. Local waiting queue loses work at preparation start; whole-process unfinished work ends at handover. Independently usable parallel preparation assumed; backlog shrinks only while completions exceed accepted arrivals.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Increase usable preparation capacity or change accepted load, then reassess the whole process.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Staff and equipment cost money. Same machine access may prevent parallel work; quality and handover capacity remain.
example_structure.evidence: Hypothetical scenario and stipulated continuation; no expected result presented as measured outcome. Qualitative ranking and ordering replace illustrative arithmetic.

visual.question: What must change to increase completed drinks?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Paid orders queue before a limiting preparation station. More ticket storage cannot prepare drinks. An independently equipped trained barista can expand preparation, after which handover may become the next limit. The local queue and whole-process unfinished orders have different exit boundaries. Change: Increase usable preparation capacity or change accepted load, then reassess the whole process. Limitation: Staff and equipment cost money. Same machine access may prevent parallel work; quality and handover capacity remain.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. Process arrows carry orders between required stages. Storage changes waiting space; usable parallel preparation changes processing capacity. The backlog shrinks only while completed handovers exceed newly accepted orders, and another constraint may appear.

patterns.evidence_boundary: Foundational definitions and formal results retain their assumptions. Empirical studies retain setting and design limitations. Examples and suggested practical responses are original editorial synthesis. Expected familiarity is an editorial judgment, not a comprehension-study finding.
